parts.text: A sky-diver jumps out of a hot-air balloon, which is 4000 m above the ground. At time = 30 s, she opens her parachute. Fig. 1.1 is the speed-time graph of her fall. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Label with the letter X the point on the graph where the sky-diver opens her parachute. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Label with the letters Y and Z the two parts of the graph where the sky-diver falls at terminal velocity. [1]

ms.label: 1(a)(ii)
ms.text: Y AND Z near any horizontal section of graph

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
any two from:
•
weight OR force of / due to gravity acts down
•
(force of / due to) air resistance / drag / friction acts up / opposes motion
•
initially / up to 10 s: resultant force is downward OR downward force is greater than upward force
•
resultant force causes acceleration
•
air resistance increases as speed increases / she accelerates
any two from:
•
acceleration (down) initially / for first 10 s
•
acceleration decreases as air resistance increases / resultant force decreases
•
zero acceleration / constant speed / terminal velocity reached when upwards force = downwards force OR when
no / zero resultant OR when forces balanced OR when downward force = air resistance
•
terminal velocity / constant speed reached after (about) 10 s OR at 60 m / s

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Calculate the average speed of the sky-diver in the first 4.0 s of her fall. average speed = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
(average speed =) {initial speed + final speed} / 2 words, symbols or numbers
OR (average speed =) distance (from area) / time words, symbols or numbers
(average speed = 40 / 2 =) 20 m / s
OR (av speed = 80 / 4 = ) 20 m / s
